newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen staying below 127.00 ahead of auction.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen staying below 127.00 ahead of auction.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract is expected to stay within a recent range at the higher end of 126 on Monday.
The contract is unlikely to fluctuate widely ahead of a 10-year JGB auction expected on Tuesday, traders said.

"I cannot see any factor providing direction to the contract today," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit. "But it seems the topside will be capped after short-covering pushed it up on Friday last week."
Traders said they expected the contract to move in a 126.60-127.00 range, against Friday' 126.85 close.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) is scheduled to start a two-day branch managers' meeting on Monday, which is also keeping the December contract from moving greatly, traders said.

"The BOJ's recent operations suggested that the bank is still cautious about the fragility of the economic recovery. If this is what the branch managers' meeting is about, that would have no impact on JGBs," said a dealer at a Big Four brokerage.

Since the new bank reserves reporting period started last Wednesday, the BOJ has been taking an accommodative credit stance. But it has varied the sum left in surplus in the market depending on the previous day's key short-term interest rates.
